title: Seat `ia preview` and `ia author` at target-owning `@workspace`, add `@mandate` `authority.words` allow-lists, and isolate oversized and high-error `.ia` sources
summary: Seat `ia preview` and `ia author` at the `@workspace` owning the target path via longest-root resolution (#285). Add optional `authority.words` allow-lists on `@schema mandate`, judged beside `authority.excluded-words` (#286): `ia preview` and `ia author` refuse a record whose word the governing mandates disallow (`IA-RUNTIME-MANDATE-WORD`), and `ia validate` reports one (`COMP-MANDATE` / `IA-COMP-MANDATE-WORD`). `COMP-MANDATE` does not judge administrative records such as a `@mandate` itself, so it does not report a widened `authority.words` on a mandate. When an authored `@hook` selects an edit to a `.ia` file under `.ia/src/`, the `steward-hook` edit guard also judges the words of the record headers (`@<word> <name>` lines) in the text the `Write`, `Edit` or `MultiEdit` writes: a new or wholly rewritten file, or an edit that adds a whole record, is checked, but an edit that changes an existing record's fields without rewriting its header line is not yet judged on words. Replace unbounded array spreads, the parser's recursive field nesting and quadratic diagnostic paths in `@inventarch/language` and `@inventarch/db`, so the oversized and high-error `.ia` sources reported in #198 now fail cleanly, naming their file, without call-stack overflow or heap exhaustion. Some recursion remains: a `requires` chain of thousands of `@system` records can still overflow the call stack and leave the workspace unreadable, as in 3.8.1.
